w:r.w:t: The BigFix client loop speed (evaluation cycle) is critical because it determines how quickly an endpoint detects changes, evaluates policy relevance, and acts on instructions. A fast, optimized loop ensures near real-time responsiveness, while a slow loop can lead to delays in patch application, slower software deployment, and less responsive reporting.

The speed of the evaluation loop directly dictates how quickly a “Take Action” command is initiated. When a policy or patch becomes relevant, the client must complete its current loop before detecting and acting on it.
The client continuously evaluates Fixlets, Tasks, and Analyses to determine applicability. A slow loop can make the client appear unresponsive and delay critical security updates.
A 15-minute average evaluation cycle is considered excellent.
A 30-minute average evaluation cycle is the benchmark threshold used in health checks before deeper investigation begins.

Cycles consistently exceeding 30 to 60 minutes typically indicate that the agent is overloaded, often due to the abuse of the Master ActionSite, too many activated Analyses, excessive site subscriptions, excessive amounts of custom analyses/properties, and/or poorly written relevance amongst any custom content.
Four Starting Points for Reviewing Loop Speed
These four areas are starting points for reviewing slow client loops. Change one thing, run the analysis again and compare the Average Loop Time tile with your Day 0 baseline.
1. Stop improper use of Master Operator (MO) accounts
In this report: Contributing Factors shows ActionSite size, master operators, their open actions and their content.
This can lead to two major problems.
Excessive ActionSite folder growth that leads to increased client processing time.

This folder contains the endpoint’s local copy of the Master Action Site, which all clients process as part of their normal evaluation cycle. If this folder exceeds 10 MB, the client may spend excessive time processing it, delaying evaluation of other content. Suggested action: Clean up actions and content associated with MO accounts and the Master Action/Operator Site. Restrict the use of MO accounts to only be used for the actual configuration of BigFix itself.
Interrupted client loops that can also lead to increased client processing time.

The BigFix client gives newly received ActionSite (also mailbox site and operator-site) versions special evaluation handling so that action-related changes can be processed and reported quickly. Suggested action: Restrict the use of MO accounts to only be used for the actual configuration of BigFix itself.
In this report: CPU Settings: CPU Idle Settings and Multicore CPU Scaling show which Clients have each setting.

The default work and sleep settings are 10 ms and 480 ms, about a 2% configured duty cycle on one core. Review the reported settings before considering changes. Refer to the task “BES Client Setting: CPU Usage” in the BES Support site.

For BigFix 11.0.7 and later, there is also Multicore CPU Scaling. The client scales its work to the number of cores at startup, so an 8-core system no longer gives the client only 0.25% of the available clock time. It right-sizes the client’s CPU use and does not raise it. It is off by default, so deploy it carefully and avoid virtual machines and critical or sensitive servers. The setting is _BESClient_Resource_ScaleWorkTimeWithCPUCores. Deploy it with the task “Enable Client CPU Multicore Scaling”.
3. Reduce content load and fix expensive content
In this report: Loop Cost: Top 10 Most Expensive Evaluations and Evaluation Frequency.
Verify the proper implementation of Anti-Virus exclusions.
Limit the number of Fixlets/Tasks, sites, computer groups, operators, and Analyses.

Determine which Fixlets, Tasks, or Analyses consume the most evaluation time and optimize or disable them as needed. There are two ways to investigate this. (1) The Client Usage Profiler tool can be used to help identify these items. This tool does a very deep dive and uploads a “package” of data to troubleshoot various issues.

(2) This report uses the “Client Performance Counters - Basic” analysis. That analysis has a property that lists the 10 most expensive evaluations on each client. Check whether each one is needed (including duplicate properties), whether it reports too often and whether it can be made more efficient.

It's easier to view this data in Web reports vs. the Console since the console shows <multiple results>. If you try to view that data using the Summary view instead of the List view just be aware the console sorts low to high. So, the results are not in a good order. Web Reports provides another view. Explore Data > Content > choose the analysis > View Computers.
Identify and adjust properties with frequent reporting intervals.

This issue is tied closely to expensive content but has a subtle difference. Properties have settings that control how often they evaluate. Some properties might need to be evaluated often like an important security setting, but many others are either not that important or just don’t change that often. So, evaluating those properties every client reporting period, each minute, etc. is wasteful and can increase loop times. The Evaluation Frequency graphic counts the properties set to every report or to under 15 minutes. That count also includes external properties, which the query below does not list.

The session relevance below identifies custom properties and properties from active custom analyses set to evaluate every report or in under 15 minutes. It does not list external properties, so it can return far fewer rows than the Evaluation Frequency count. Change the evaluation period on the last line to adjust the query.
exists active flags whose (it) of activations
(not exists evaluation period of it OR evaluation period of it < 15 * minute)
4. If UDP is blocked, set Command Polling
In this report: Notification and Polling: UDP Notification Coverage, Command Polling and Reported Polling Checks.

When clients do not receive UDP notifications and the firewall is out of your hands, Command Polling is the workaround. Deploy the task “Set Command Polling to 10 Minutes over Average Evaluation Time”.
